Name: Prohibiting the operation of class three bicycles with electric assist.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to prohibiting the operation of class three bicycles with electric assist

Summary: This bill would prohibit the operation of class three bicycles with electric assist on city streets, in parks, and in other public places. For violations occurring before December 1, 2029, violators would receive a warning and relevant information concerning the law. Beginning on December 1, 2029, violators would be liable for civil penalties in increasing amounts: $0 for the first violation, $50 for the second violation, and $200 for any subsequent violation.
Text:
Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subchapter 3 of chapter 1 of title 19 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 19-176.4 to read as follows:
19-176.4 Class three bicycles with electric assist. a. Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following terms have the following meanings:
Class three bicycle with electric assist. The term “class three bicycle with electric assist” has the same meaning as set forth in subdivision (c) of section 102-c of the vehicle and traffic law.
Designated citywide languages. The term “designated citywide languages” has the same meaning as set forth in section 23-1101.
b. No person shall operate a class three bicycle with electric assist on streets or in parks or other public places in the city of New York.
c. Authorized employees of the police department and department of parks and recreation shall have the authority to enforce the provisions of this section.
d. A person who violates subdivision b of this section prior to December 1, 2029, shall not be issued a notice of violation, but shall be issued a warning. Any such warning shall inform such person that the authorized employee of the police department or department of parks and recreation issuing such warning believes such person has violated subdivision b of this section, and shall advise such person that the law authorizes civil penalties for such a violation occurring on or after December 1, 2029, and that subsequent violations occurring on or after such date may result in the imposition of such civil penalties. Such warning shall inform such person of the written materials developed pursuant to subdivision f of this section and describe how such person may access such materials.
e. A person who violates subdivision b of this section on or after December 1, 2029, shall be liable as follows: 
1. For a first violation, a civil penalty of $0 dollars; 
2. For a second violation issued on a different date than the date of a first violation, a civil penalty of not more than $50; and
3. For each subsequent violation issued on a different date than the date of a first violation or a second violation, a civil penalty of not more than $200.
f. The commissioner, in consultation with any agency head the commissioner deems relevant, shall develop written materials advising an owner of a class three bicycle with electric assist of their rights and responsibilities under this section and of how such an owner may comply with this section. Such written materials shall be made available on the department’s website no later than June 1, 2029.
g. The commissioner shall conduct culturally appropriate outreach in the designated citywide languages to advise owners of class three bicycles with electric assist of their rights and responsibilities under this section and of the availability of the written materials developed pursuant to subdivision f of this section
§ 2. This local law takes effect 30 months after it becomes law.
